summary: The bill amends the FY2021 NDAA to bar any U.S. institution of higher education from receiving federal research and development awards for five years after it accepts funding from the governments of China, Russia, Iran, or other listed countries (or their agents) for national-security-related work in artificial intelligence, biotechnology, or quantum information science.

scores.thoughts: The bill prohibits certain higher education institutions from receiving federal research and development awards (government-funded grants) for five years if they accept funding from specified foreign sources for sensitive national security-related research. This directly restricts eligibility for federal expenditures, producing a minor reduction in the scope of government spending on R&D.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms or gun regulations.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration, visas, or border policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion or reproductive rights.

The bill amends the NDAA and restricts R&D awards tied to national security or military applications (AI, biotechnology, quantum information science). By narrowing eligibility for such defense-related research funding, it produces a minor decrease in defense R&D spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to environmental regulations or climate policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs or social safety-net spending.

The bill directly limits federal R&D awards to institutions of higher education that accept funding from listed foreign governments for specified research tasks. This restricts federal involvement and public investment in university research, producing a moderate negative effect on the education topic.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement or decriminalization.
The bill contains no provisions related to criminal sentencing, policing, or justice reform.
The bill contains no provisions related to tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
By restricting eligibility for certain federal R&D awards, the bill produces a very minor reduction in government outlays and therefore leans slightly toward prioritizing debt reduction.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections.
The bill contains no provisions related to U.S. foreign aid disbursements.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access or election integrity.
The bill references AI and quantum information science only in the context of restricting foreign-funded research at universities; it does not regulate technology companies or privacy protections.
The bill contains no provisions related to unions or worker protections.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
